The three-kingdom system placed prokaryotes in Protista and continued to include fungi in Plantae, despite fungi being heterotrophs that absorb nutrients and having chitin rather than cellulose in their cell walls.
The Linnaean system arranges organisms in a hierarchy of seven ranks, from the broadest to the most specific: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species.

Incorrect classification can lead to mistaken conclusions about an organism’s characteristics and relationships, misdirect conservation efforts, and make scientific research and communication less accurate.
